Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: Participants self-reported their height and weight on open-ended items. We standardized this data so as to present height in meters and weight in kilogrammes, and self-reported BMI was subsequently computed as kg/m^2.

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes how BMI was derived from participants' self-reported height and weight, with values standardized to meters and kilograms and BMI computed as kg/m^2. It notes that improbable BMI values (< 12 or > 50 kg/m^2) were replaced using a mean replacement method (< 4.0% of the dataset) and that self-reported height and weight correlate strongly with measured data. The section does not mention any study numbering, sample size, demographics, body appreciation assessment, or correlations between body appreciation and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: Participants self-reported their height and weight on open-ended items. We standardized this data so as to present height in meters and weight in kilogrammes, and self-reported BMI was subsequently computed as kg/m^2. Where computations resulted in improbable BMI values (< 12 or > 50 kg/m^2), we replaced these using the mean replacement method (< 4.0% of the total dataset). Self-reported height and weight data are strongly correlated with measured data and can be reliably used in population studies (Spencer, Appleby, Davey, & Key, 2002).
